answer: Each identity adopts one distinct navigation buoy assigned from a vault registry and services it monthly: a boat leaves the wharf, crews swap its battery, and verifiers match AIS position, its key-seeded light pattern and photos of hull fouling against the prior record. A buoy on a tundra coast must survive winter ice, logged by its tilt sensor. One crew services at most 6 buoys daily, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 buoys at $340 monthly each ($340,000 monthly) plus boats; a shared, moved or dark buoy revokes the slot. Trade-off: storm weeks pause checks rather than penalising honest keepers.
